key_insight: Agentic (multi‑agent) AI systems must include explicit transparency—clear motivations, explanations, and reporting—when embedded in scientific workflows to avoid wasting computational and human resources.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap of insufficient transparency and justification in multi‑agent/agentic AI deployments that can lead to inefficiency, reproducibility problems, wasted compute, and unnecessary human effort in research settings.
method: Survey and analyze common agentic AI frameworks to identify where transparency breaks down in research workflows.
Propose practical transparency principles and a reporting checklist for when and how to deploy agentic components.
Recommend evaluation metrics and human‑in‑the‑loop protocols to justify agent use and track resource and outcome impacts.
impact: Provides researchers and practitioners concise guidance to decide whether and how to use agentic systems responsibly, reducing wasted resources and improving reproducibility, trust, and stewardship of compute and human effort.
visual_elements: Layered diagram of a multi‑agent system with highlighted ‘transparency checkpoints’ (motivation, inputs, objectives, outputs, logs).
Decision flowchart for ‘Should you deploy an agent?’ showing criteria and gating questions (cost, benefit, explainability, oversight).
Side‑by‑side bar chart comparing compute/human cost and reproducibility outcomes with vs without transparency measures.
One‑page checklist infographic summarizing reporting requirements and evaluation metrics for agentic deployments.
